title: Twenty-two Winters and One Extra Chair
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（生活与学习·家庭生活）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（生活与学习·家庭生活）　|　核心词汇：dinner　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dinner 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1945 my grandmother ① gave a dinner that no neighbour in the lane would have forgotten, and she said the giving was the whole of the winter. The ② dinner, meaning the meal and not the occasion, ran twenty-two winters and stayed unmentioned in the letters; a dinner, she said, is the only thing in a family that is judged by how long it is left untalked about.

Every ③ dinner in that house had the same extra chair at the end of it, and the ④ dinner at the end, meaning the one they kept for the absent sons and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever waited for twice. A dinner, my mother said, is nine parts waiting and one part somebody willing to cook; my grandmother said the cooking is the part that fills twenty-two winters.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dinner was the whole of the year, meaning the occasion and not the meal. The ⑥ dinner, meaning the occasion and not any of that, is the only thing in a year that everybody prepares and nobody enjoys; dinner, he said, is either something you give or the only word that means both a meal and an occasion. He said the occasion is the part they remember.

By 1954 the ⑦ dinner had become a line in a diary, and the diary had become an argument about the extra chair. The ⑧ dinner of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one house and twenty-two winters of cooking; dinner, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to cook. She said the cooking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dinner I remember is the one at the end, which was eaten in 1971 and is still described as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ dinner, my mother said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being shared; every dinner, she said, is an occasion that has agreed to look like a meal. She said the occasion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 晚餐；正餐（指家里摆出的那一顿）
B. n. 正餐（指那顿饭本身，与那个场合相对）
C. 固定搭配：give a dinner 设一席正餐
D. n. 正餐（指留给不在家的儿子们用的那一顿）
E. n. 正餐；饭食（抽象总称，指一家人的全部饭桌之事）
F. n. 正餐（指日记里写到、被记下的那一顿）
G. n. 宴会；聚餐场合（指一年里操办的那场聚会）
H. n. 场合（抽象总称，指人人操办却无人尽兴的那场）

items.q: gave a dinner that no neighbour in the lane would have forgotten
The dinner, meaning the meal and not the occasion
the dinner was the whole of the year
the dinner had become a line in a diary
The dinner of the whole thing
A dinner, my mother said in 1973

answers.why: give a dinner 意为“设一席正餐”，1945 年祖母设了一席巷子里没有一位邻居会忘记的正餐。
dinner 意为“正餐”，指那顿饭本身而不是那个场合，它历经二十二个冬天而在家书里无人提起。
dinner 意为“晚餐、正餐”，指那栋房子里每一顿正餐，每一顿末尾都摆着同一把多出来的椅子。
dinner 意为“正餐”，指留给不在家的儿子们用的那一顿，是唯一有人等过两次的。
dinner 意为“宴会、聚餐场合”，指一年里操办的那场聚会，父亲说这场聚会就是那一年的全部。
dinner 意为“场合”，指人人操办却无人尽兴的那场而不是那顿饭本身，是一年里人人都操办、却无人尽兴的东西。
dinner 意为“正餐”，指日记里写到、被记下的那一顿，到 1954 年这顿正餐成了日记里的一行。
dinner 意为“正餐、饭食”，祖母一月写道，整件事的饭桌之事是一栋房子和二十二个冬天的烹饪。
dinner 意为“正餐”，我记得的是末尾那一顿，1971 年吃上的，至今仍被说成屋里最安静的一顿。
dinner 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，一顿正餐是唯一会因为被分享而变得更好的东西。
